summary: First 3-second hook fails on Reels (77% drop); zero engagement on LinkedIn/Bluesky; no DMs yet. Bio violates rules: niche/region targeting, 24hr claim, free offer outside website posts.
guidance:
- Rotate hook styles: try "top3" or "contrast" next; avoid "curiosity" (0.07x) and repeated "question" angles on chatbots.
- Stop repeating "same 5 questions" / "2 AM leads" chatbot tropes; they've appeared 4+ times.
- Keep posts sounding like a developer sharing real work: show code snippets, config decisions, or site structure — never "buy my service" language.
- Use varied Indian business examples (cafe in Kochi, gym in Jaipur, clinic in Guwahati) in one line max.
- Only offer "pay after approval" + a short DM conversation; free 3-point site check only in website posts.

instructions.research: Find 3 common website trust gaps for Indian small businesses (e.g., missing contact page, no SSL, slow mobile load) without naming specific clients.
instructions.analysis: Compare today's website post idea against the last website post (WhatsApp vs one-page site) to avoid repeating the same contrast hook.
instructions.writer: Write a Myth Bust hook for website development: bust the myth 'My WhatsApp Business profile is enough' using a contrast structure, end with 'pay after approval' CTA.
instructions.image: Create a simple split graphic: left side WhatsApp chat screen, right side a clean one-page site wireframe; no branding, just UI patterns.
instructions.video: Skip video today; static image performs better for website topics per current data.

Comment thoughtfully on 5 posts by Indian small business owners (cafes, gyms, clinics) about their online presence — no pitching.
